title: At-Risk Account Intervention Checklist & Tactical Save Plays
content:
Purpose:
This working doc is a tactical checklist and set of short-form playbooks for intervening on at-risk accounts in the 90-day window before renewal. It is intended for CSMs, AMs, and CS leadership to run structured 30/60/90 day intervention sprints, escalate effectively to execs, and execute tested save plays while preserving revenue and relationships.

Context & assumptions:
- Scope: mid-market to enterprise customers on Redwood Hosted and Dedicated tiers.
- Use when a customer meets >=2 high-risk signals (see Signals section) or when renewal likelihood < 50% in the CRM.
- This doc is intentionally lean — copy templates into PS notes, Jira tickets, or customer-facing decks as needed.

Key signals (trigger set):
- Usage drop: 30%+ decline in average monthly tokens or API calls vs prior quarter.
- Feature regression: critical features (streaming, dedicated routes, private VPC) failing or high error rates (>3% 7-day).
- Financial flag: overdue invoices >30 days or procurement stalls past PO deadline.
- Sentiment: NPS follow-up negative + no response to outreach in 14 days.
- Product fit: repeated quality regressions (inference latency up 2x or cost per 1k tokens up >25%).

Triage (first 72 hours) — rapid diagnostic probe:
1) Owner: Assigned CSM (or AM) creates a triage ticket in JIRA (link template) and tags solutions-engineering and SRE.
2) Quick health snapshot (CSM):
   - Top 3 usage metrics (tokens/day, response latency p95, error rate).
   - Support ticket count and severity in last 30 days.
   - Billing status and contract renewal date.
3) Outreach: Send templated "We see activity change" email (template below) and schedule a 30-minute discovery call within 3 business days.
4) Diagnostic asks to customer: consent for brief logs/KV cache diagnostics, permission to run traffic replay (if Dedicated/Private).

30-day recovery sprint — prioritized plays (ordered):
- Play A: Engagement Reset (low friction) — owner: CSM
  Actions: deep discovery call, bring in Solutions AE for ROI refresh, share tailored usage dashboard, set 2-week checkpoints.
  Success metric: scheduled renewal conversation + concrete commitment on next actions.

- Play B: Technical Rescue (medium friction) — owner: Solutions Engineering + SRE
  Actions: hotfix or config change (batching tweaks, quantization profile update), temporary routing to a stable model variant, priority support escalation SLA, run smoke tests and provide metrics within 48 hours.
  Budget/Approval: may need PS hours; pre-approve small contingency credit (see offers below).

- Play C: Commercial Bridge (higher friction) — owner: AM + RevOps
  Actions: propose temporary credit/discount tied to performance SLAs, restructure billing cadence, or pilot Dedicated capacity for a fixed period.
  Approval process: small offers (<= $10k) approved by AM lead; >$10k requires RevOps sign-off.

60-day escalation matrix (if 30-day plays inadequate):
- Condition: No booking commitment and risk remains high.
- Steps:
  1) Prepare Exec Brief (one-pager) — include health metrics, timeline of actions, customer exec contact, concrete ask (e.g., PO by date or trial extension + credit).
  2) Trigger: CSM requests Exec Sync with CS Director and Customer Exec Sponsor.
  3) Offer: introduce "Recovery Runway" package — 90-day focused support, weekly ops reviews, up to 40 hours of Solutions Eng dedicated time, and a conditional discount if SLAs not met.

Exec escalation template (email subject + body):
- Subject: "[Action requested] Exec-sync request: <Customer> renewal at risk (Renewal: YYYY-MM-DD)"
- Body (short):
  Hi <LeaderName>,

  Quick brief: <Customer> (ARR $X, Tier) is at elevated renewal risk. Key signals: 35% usage drop, p95 latency 3.2s, billing dispute open.
  Actions taken: discovery call (MM/DD), technical hotfix deployed (MM/DD), offered short-term credits.
  Ask: Exec intro to <Customer Exec> this week to align on procurement timeline and approve Recovery Runway.

  Attach: one-page PDF (health snapshot + timeline).

  Thanks,
  <CSM Name>

Save plays & acceptable concession ladder (ordered lowest to highest cost):
1) Free concierge onboarding hours (up to 8 hours) + priority triage.
2) Short-term credit (1–2 weeks) applied to next invoice for platform instability.
3) Performance SLA addendum (trial) — guarantee latency/cost targets for 60 days or credit.
4) Discount on renewal / usage rebate (sliding scale tied to adoption recovery).
5) Contract restructure (term change, capacity swap) — escalation to RevOps/Legal.

Customer-facing templates (short versions to paste into email thread):
- Engagement Reset invite: "Hi <Name>, we noticed platform usage dip and want to make sure everything is working for you. Can we schedule a 30m call this week to align on immediate needs and a recovery plan? — <CSM>"
- Technical Rescue note: "We deployed a config change to your route and temporarily routed traffic to variant X. Please validate and share logs; we'll follow up in 48h with metrics."
- Recovery Runway offer: "We can provide a 90-day Recovery Runway: weekly ops calls, dedicated engineering hours, and a conditional credit if we miss agreed SLAs. Would you be open to a 2-week pilot?"

Internal checklist for the save sprint (CSM to tick off):
- [ ] Create triage JIRA ticket and add linked artifacts
- [ ] Pull last 90 days usage + trend chart into shared deck
- [ ] Schedule discovery call + invite Solutions Eng if needed
- [ ] Post-call: update CRM with risk score and next steps
- [ ] If technical: open support priority case and request SRE attention
- [ ] If commercial: build offer + get approval from RevOps
- [ ] Draft exec brief if no progress by day 30
- [ ] Run weekly stakeholder syncs and log meeting notes in drive

Measuring success (KPIs for the intervention):
- Renewal outcome: renewed vs churned (primary)
- Time to commit: days from triage to signed commitment
- Health delta: % improvement in key metrics (tokens/day, p95 latency) at 30/60/90 days
- Customer satisfaction: follow-up CSAT or NPS change

Knowledge nuggets & playbook notes (lessons from saves):
- Fast technical wins often stem from routing to an older stable model variant and rolling config changes (less risky than immediate quantization swaps).
- Commercial concessions tied to measurable recovery milestones preserve ARR better than unconditional discounts.
- Exec-to-exec conversations are most effective when coupled with a concrete narrow ask (approve X hours / PO by date).

Next steps / TODOs for this doc:
- Convert templates into CRM email snippets and add to the CSM playbook kit (owner: Maya).
- Add standard Recovery Runway contract appendix for legal (owner: RevOps).
- Create automation: alert to create triage JIRA when "usage drop" and "billing flag" co-occur (owner: Eng-Observability).

Notes: this is a living doc — copy/adapt flows to customer scale and contract complexity. If you run a save and it worked, paste a short case summary under "saves-directory" so we can sharpen offers and timelines.
